theses.subject: Memory, HBM & Storage
theses.thesis: Memory/HBM is the rank-1 leader with the highest score and is eligible (trend gate passed; hurst_tag 'trend'). It is NOT crowded (crowding_z 0.86), which historically is the texture that survives shake-outs better. However r10 is negative (-0.159) and val_state is 'diverging', which is a caution on breadth/cohesion rather than a fade trigger.
theses.dissent: Negative r10 and a diverging value state indicate the theme may already be losing internal breadth even as the composite score stays high — classic late-stage leadership that can roll over without a crowding signal.

falsifier.text: SMH lags the S&P 500 by 5% or more over any consecutive 10-trading-day window before the check-by date.

theses.subject: Non-AI Software
theses.thesis: Non-AI Software is the rank-2 challenger, trend-tagged and eligible, with the strongest durability_bar (0.59) among the top themes, suggesting the trend leg is actually more persistent than the leader's. It is flagged crowded (crowding_z 1.39), which means size-down caution only — not a reason to avoid the direction itself.
theses.dissent: A crowding flag on a trend means any wobble can trigger fast de-grossing; reflexive positioning can reverse quickly even if the fundamental trend is intact.

falsifier.text: IGV underperforms SMH by more than 4% cumulative while SMH remains above trend, before the check-by date.

theses.subject: Cybersecurity
theses.thesis: Cybersecurity ranks third, is trend-tagged, and is eligible with the highest durability_bar (0.68) in the entire table. The elevated crowding_z (1.65) argues for cap/size-down not avoidance. This is a durability story: strongest staying-power leg among all scorable themes.
theses.dissent: Being the most crowded theme in a detector whose crowd metric has no forward edge means a sudden unwind could be sharp and unrelated to trend health.

falsifier.text: CIBR breaks below its 50-day moving average while the S&P 500 holds above its own, before the check-by date.
